checks.invariant: A repos[].path read from .agents/ultrapowers.json stays inside the project root before the preflight walks it, reads its manifests and hands it on as the repository folder
checks.result: readProject keeps text(r.path) as written and checks only that name and path are non-empty (hunt-files.mjs:59). loadProject validates only the ticket (hunt-preflight.mjs:518-537). preflight() then runs resolve(root, repo.path) (:564), which accepts an absolute path or '..' segments, and the result goes to walk(), declaredFacts() and (full mode) the SCOPE tree: lines. The path is checked for existence only (:565). The template ships only a relative nested path. Nothing in the three files bounds it. Sibling control: repo names are validated (:553, hunt-sandbox.mjs:263), paths are not.

checks.invariant: The sandbox's bind source, the sandbox image and the limits that come from the config are bounded before they reach docker run (h2 owns the docker argument internals; this check covers only the config-to-sink trust)
checks.result: Image: PINNED digest, --pull=never and a local-cache check in probe (:99-104) bound hunt.sandbox.images, so the audited config cannot select an arbitrary image. Limits: LIMIT_RULES validators (:68-70) bound hunt.sandbox.limits. Mount source: runCheck sets repoDir = resolve(root, entry.path) (:325) with no containment check and dockerArgs binds it read-only as source=<repoDir> (:130). A path outside the project would therefore be mounted into the container that runs target code, and the key-material masks are computed only inside that directory (maskPaths(repoDir), :115-121). This is the one config value reaching a sink as trusted input.

checks.invariant: Every cell of a DECLARED row that comes from the audited tree is a plain name or version, so tree text never rides to the unguarded research subagent
checks.result: The subject and version are filtered hard: safeCell on the raw strings, then PLAIN_SUBJECT and plainVersion on the stripUrl output (hunt-preflight.mjs:136-145,170). The file:line cell is not. `where` = `${file}:${line}` (:166) is checked only by safeCell(where) at :170, which rejects control characters, a backtick, `$(` and more than 200 characters. A file path may hold spaces, letters and most punctuation. walk() returns every real path (hunt-files.mjs:30-31) and render() prints the cell through printable(), which escapes only those same characters (:614-617,632). A row with a plain dependency such as good@1.0.0 in a package.json under a directory named like a sentence therefore prints the sentence as the file:line cell. The comment at :132-135 says a manifest string never rides in a row as text, but this cell does. The existing tests cover subject and version cells only and none cover the path cell (tests/vulnerability-hunt/hunt-preflight.test.mjs:669-790).

checks.invariant: The consumer of DECLARED has a deterministic control, not only a prompt, between tree text and its tools
checks.result: research.md:22-27 and vulnerability-hunter.md:120-124 hand the rows to a subagent that has the session's tools and no guardrail, 'unchanged'. The only control on the file:line cell is the prompt sentence telling it to treat an instruction-like row as data. The agent file states the reason itself: 'the step has the session's tools and no guardrail'. A prompt is not a boundary. The deterministic filter the design relies on is the one that misses this cell.

checks.invariant: Every file the ticket's change set touches appears in the SCOPE file: lines, whatever the file is named
checks.result: changedFiles runs `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d <base><sep><branch>` with no -z and no -c core.quotepath=false (hunt-preflight.mjs:505). childEnv adds nothing git-related (resolve-tool.mjs:56-58). Git quotes such names by default: a path with a non-ASCII byte, a double quote, a backslash or a control character is printed as a double-quoted C-escaped string. The result is split on newlines (:506) and then filtered with existsSync(join(repoDir, f)) (:580). A quoted name is not a path on disk, so it is dropped with no note and no count. The rendered file: lines (:625), the SCOPE file count, the lane decision from `files.length` (:408-409) and the `scope_paths` of the Cloudflare run all omit that changed file. A ticket-scoped hunt (the default depth is quick) can then report on a change set that leaves out the file the author named in a non-ASCII way. Full-audit mode uses walk() and is not affected. Not observed: the sandbox is unavailable and the preflight was not run.

checks.invariant: A ref or branch name that reaches git argv, and the review-preflight output that carries ranges, cannot be read as an option or forge a range
checks.result: The base is repos[].defaultBranch from the config (qa-preflight.mjs:266, default 'main'). It goes unvalidated into the argument `${base}...${branch}` with no `--` or --end-of-options (hunt-preflight.mjs:505; the same shape is in qa-preflight.mjs:224-237). A base starting with `--output=` would be taken as git's --output option and write the name list to a file whose name ends in `...<branch>`. The suffix keeps it from naming a useful file, so the impact is nil and this is hardening only. The branch half comes from rev-parse and is filtered by the ticket regex, and it is not in an option position. The ticket id passed to bash is validated (no leading '-', no whitespace, hunt-preflight.mjs:530). A forged RANGES section cannot come from DOCS: the awk filter in review-preflight.sh:36 prints only lines of the form `<n> bytes`. One side effect: ticketRanges aborts on any line containing 'ERROR' anywhere in review-preflight output (hunt-preflight.mjs:483), so a doc path containing that word stops the hunt. That is fail-closed.

candidates.title: A changed file with a non-ASCII or special-character name silently drops out of the ticket-scoped hunt
candidates.description: In a ticket-scoped hunt, changedFiles reads `git diff --name-only` without -z and without disabling core.quotepath. Git prints a changed path that holds a non-ASCII byte, a double quote, a backslash or a control character as a quoted, escaped string. The preflight then keeps only names for which existsSync(join(repoDir, name)) is true. The quoted string is not a path on disk, so the file is dropped with no note or count. The author of the audited branch controls file names. A changed file with such a name is absent from the SCOPE file: lines, the file count, the lane decisions and the Cloudflare `scope_paths`, so the hunt's verdict can describe a change set that omits that file.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The path list is parsed from newline-separated git output that quotes unusual names, and an existence filter then discards what it cannot resolve, silently and without -z.

trace.description: git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d <base>...<branch> is spawned with no -z and no -c core.quotepath=false, so names with unusual bytes are quoted by git.
stdout is split on newlines and kept as the list of changed paths, quoted forms included.
The list is filtered by existsSync(join(repoDir, f)); a quoted name does not exist on disk, so the file is removed from the scope with no note.
Only the surviving names are printed as SCOPE file: lines, which the overlay uses as the run's scope_paths, so the omitted file is never audited.

evidence.description: childEnv adds only NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath on Windows and sets no git quoting configuration.
The tests check hostile names in manifest cells; none puts a quoted-name file in a ticket change set.

blockers: The sandbox is unavailable for this run and the preflight was not run, so git's quoting of such a name in a ticket-branch diff was not observed.
Whether the user's or system git config sets core.quotepath=false is a deployment fact outside source; the default is true.

validation_plan.local: In a dummy repository, commit a file named with a non-ASCII character or a double quote on a ticket branch and run hunt-preflight.mjs for that ticket. Confirm the file is missing from SCOPE file: lines and from the count. Then compare against `git diff --name-only -z`. Fix: pass -z (or -c core.quotepath=false and a literal parse), split on NUL, and report a changed path that does not exist on disk in a note instead of dropping it.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner may run git config --get core.quotepath on the machines that run hunts to see whether the default has been changed.

candidates.title: The file:line cell of a DECLARED row carries free-text file paths from the audited tree to the unguarded research subagent
candidates.description: The preflight keeps a DECLARED row only if its subject and version are plain, and a comment says no manifest string rides in a row as text. The fifth cell, `file:line`, is the manifest's repository path, and it gets a weaker check: no control character, backtick or `$(`, and at most 200 characters. A file path can hold spaces and arbitrary punctuation. A branch author who adds `<sentence-like directory name>/package.json` with one harmless dependency therefore gets the directory name printed in the row and passed unchanged to the research subagent. That subagent has the session's tools and no guardrail, and its only control on instruction-like rows is a sentence in its prompt.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: Subject and version are filtered with plain-name allow-lists; the path cell is filtered with a deny-list of control characters, backtick and `$(` only, although it is the same kind of untrusted tree text going to the same unguarded consumer.

trace.description: Every real file path of the audited repository, including directory names the author chose, is returned as a relative path.
where = `${file}:${line}` is built from that path.
safeCell(where) is the only test on the path cell; PLAIN_SUBJECT and plainVersion apply to subject and version alone.
printable escapes only control characters, backtick and `$(`, so spaces and prose pass.
The cell is printed in the DECLARED section, which STEP 0b passes unchanged as <DECLARED> to a research subagent that has the session's tools and no guardrail (prompts/research.md:22-27).

evidence.description: The comment states the design intent: a manifest string never rides in a row as text, and a non-plain row is dropped.
The contract says the research step has the session's tools and no guardrail, and relies on the preflight dropping non-plain rows.
The prompt's own defence is an instruction to report an instruction-like row in `reason` and not follow it, which is not a deterministic control.

blockers: The sandbox is unavailable for this run and the preflight was not run, so the printed row with a prose path was not observed.
That the research subagent acts on such text with its tools is model behaviour and a harness fact (its tool set, whether it can run commands or send queries) that source cannot settle.

validation_plan.local: In a dummy repository, create a directory whose name is a harmless sentence containing a spaced phrase, put a package.json with one plain dependency inside it, and run hunt-preflight.mjs --full-audit. Confirm the DECLARED row prints the sentence in the file:line cell. Fix: apply the plain-name allow-list to the path cell too (for example drop the row, or print a hash of the path and the line only), and add a test beside tests/vulnerability-hunt/hunt-preflight.test.mjs:669.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner may check the tool set the STEP 0b research subagent receives on each harness (shell, web fetch) to size the impact. No live probe is needed.

candidates.title: repos[].path from the audited branch's config is not bounded to the project root before it is walked and bind-mounted
candidates.description: readProject accepts any non-empty repos[].path. The preflight and the sandbox runner resolve it with resolve(root, path), which allows absolute paths and '..' segments. The preflight walks the result, reads its manifests and, in a full audit, prints its top-level folders. The runner binds the same directory read-only into the container that runs target code. If the checked-out branch can change .agents/ultrapowers.json, which the architecture lists as audited-tree data, a branch author can point a repository outside the project and so give the hunt, and the sandbox that runs agent-chosen commands, a view of host files that are not part of the project. The image (digest-pinned, --pull=never) and the limits (validated) are bounded; the path is not.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: The config reader validates the repository name but not the path, so a value the audited tree can alter reaches the walk and the docker bind source as trusted input.

trace.description: repos[].path is read with text(r.path) from .agents/ultrapowers.json and kept as written; only emptiness is checked.
repoDir = resolve(root, repo.path) with no containment test; only existsSync is checked.
walk(repoDir), manifestsFromFiles and declaredFacts read the directory, and a full audit prints its top-level folders as tree: lines.
repoDir = resolve(root, entry.path) is bound read-only as /target (dockerArgs, line 130) into the container that runs the target's code (h2 owns the docker internals).

evidence.description: Control on the image: a digest pin, a local-cache check and --pull=never (line 128) bound the image; nothing equivalent exists for the path.
The scaffold writes nested relative repository paths, so a path outside the project is not part of the shipped layout.

blockers: Whether the audited branch's .agents/ultrapowers.json is the effective config of a hunt (a pull request branch checked out in the root) is a deployment fact outside source.
The sandbox is unavailable for this run, so no mount was observed.
Which host files a hunter or a container command could then read depends on the guardrail's read rules (h1) and the sandbox masks (h2), which are outside this unit.

validation_plan.local: In a dummy project, set a repos[].path to '..' or an absolute dummy folder, run hunt-preflight.mjs --full-audit and confirm the dummy folder is walked and its folders printed. In the sandbox, once available, confirm that dockerArgs binds that folder. Fix: refuse any path whose realpath is not inside the realpath of the project root, in readProject, so both consumers share the check.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner may confirm whether hunts are run on a pull request branch checked out in the project root, so that its config applies. If configs are always taken from the trusted base branch, this is hardening only.

hardening: Revision arguments reach git as `${base}...${branch}` with no `--` or --end-of-options (hunt-preflight.mjs:505; qa-preflight.mjs:224-237). A config defaultBranch starting with `--output=` is read as an option. The suffix `...<branch>` keeps the written file name useless, so the impact is nil, but the shape is wrong. Fix: validate refs with `git check-ref-format --branch` or pass `--end-of-options`.

ticketRanges aborts on any line containing 'ERROR' in review-preflight.sh output (hunt-preflight.mjs:483), including DOCS lines made of file names from the audited tree. A doc path containing the word stops the hunt. This fails closed, but it is a spurious denial a branch author can cause.

walk() skips folders named build, dist, node_modules and .git at any depth (hunt-files.mjs:10,28). In a full audit, hand-written code or manifests under a folder named build/ (build scripts are common) are outside the SCOPE tree: groups, the manifests and DECLARED. Ticket mode is unaffected because git decides the scope.

The public/private flag on a DECLARED row derives from tree data (a .npmrc registry line, lockfile resolved hosts, a git or URL spec). A branch author can mark a vulnerable dependency private so STEP 0b skips it. Dependencies with an installed audit tool are covered by that tool, which limits the impact.

ticketPattern from the config goes to new RegExp (hunt-preflight.mjs:533) and a configured pattern that is invalid throws an uncaught SyntaxError instead of a Failure. The input is the short ticket id, so there is no ReDoS concern worth a candidate.

declaredFacts reads every file of the tree up to 2 MiB (hunt-preflight.mjs:179) and re-reads sibling requirements files per file (:247). These are local same-user availability costs and are not reported.

uncovered.reason: The hunt's ticket scope takes its base and branch from this unchanged-in-range script, which the ledger lists neither as changed nor as prior coverage. The unvalidated defaultBranch reaches git there before it reaches changedFiles, so it needs its own deterministic unit.
